answer: A vouching bond resists sybils well: no new agent identity may transact until an already-trusted agent locks collateral behind it, and that collateral burns if the newcomer proves to be a duplicate persona. Since every fresh key needs a sponsor with real value at risk, mass-registering thousands of fakes becomes costly instead of free. A lone comet of a wallet can appear overnight, but it cannot forge a chain of sponsors willing to bleed for it. Reputation travels along those bonds, so the voyage from stranger to trusted member is earned step by step.
